os.title: Silqhaus OS
os.desc: Off-the-shelf property software was never built for how we work, so we built our own. Silqhaus OS runs every property, task, booking, and payout in one place — the backbone that Mali, the staff app, and your owner portal all plug into. One system, one source of truth, tuned exactly to our operation.

mali.title: Mali, your 24/7 guest manager
mali.desc: Most AI answers once and forgets the thread. faq.title: Your questions, answered honestly.
faq.description: The things owners actually ask us — fees, care, technology, and getting started. If yours isn't here, call and a real person will answer.

q1.a: Two plans, one simple rule — we only earn when you do. Revenue & Marketing management is 10% of rental revenue: we run your pricing, marketing, listings, and guest bookings while your own team cares for the home. Full property management is 25%: we run everything, end to end.

q2.q: What's the difference between the two plans?
q2.a: With the 10% plan you keep your own on-the-ground staff and we bring the demand — dynamic pricing, distribution across every major platform, marketing, and 24/7 guest communication. The 25% plan adds complete care of the home itself: housekeeping, maintenance, inspections, and compliance, all photo-verified.

q3.q: Are there any setup or hidden fees?
q3.a: No setup fee, no monthly retainer, no surprise charges. Our commission is performance-based — if your villa doesn't earn, we don't either.

q4.q: When and how do I get paid?
q4.a: Statements close at month-end and payouts land in your account between the 1st and 5th of the following month. Every line is visible in your owner portal long before the statement arrives.

q5.q: Who pays for repairs and supplies?
q5.a: Owners cover materials and third-party costs at cost — no markups. Every job is logged with photos and receipts in your portal, and anything beyond an agreed threshold is approved by you first.

q6.q: Do I pay anything when the calendar is empty?
q6.a: No. We charge a percentage of actual rental revenue — an empty month costs you nothing.

q7.a: Yes. Many owners start with Revenue & Marketing at 10% and move to full management at 25% once they've seen how we work. Switching is a conversation, not a contract fight.

q1.a: Ask for a free revenue estimate — no cost, no commitment. If the numbers make sense, we visit your villa, agree a plan, and have you listed and earning within about a week: photography, listings, pricing, everything.

q2.a: Phuket and Pattaya today, with expansion across Thailand underway. If your villa is elsewhere in the country, talk to us — we may be closer than you think.

q3.q: My villa has never been rented — can you set it up from zero?
q3.a: Yes. We handle professional photography, listing copy, amenity setup, pricing, and guidance through local licensing requirements — from empty house to first booking.

q4.q: Can I still use my villa myself?
q4.a: Of course — it's your home. Block any dates you want in the owner portal, and we'll work bookings around your stays.

q5.a: No — we're small by design. We assess every home first, because our promise is to run a few villas brilliantly rather than many badly.

q6.a: Flexible terms with a fair notice period, not a multi-year lock-in. We'd rather keep you with results than with paperwork.

q7.q: I live abroad — is that a problem?
q7.a: Most of our owners do. The portal keeps you connected in real time from anywhere, payouts arrive wherever you bank, and nothing about your home requires you to be in Thailand.

q1.q: How do you keep my home in top condition?
q1.a: Every job — cleaning, maintenance, inspections — is logged in our staff app with before-and-after photos, timestamps, and the name of who did it. Quality is verifiable, not just promised.

q2.a: Mali, our AI guest manager, answers instantly 24/7 in any language — and our Thai team on the ground handles everything a screen can't, with hotel standards.

q3.q: What happens if a guest damages something?
q3.a: We document everything, claim through the booking platform's damage protection or the deposit, and manage the repair ourselves. You see the full record — photos, costs, and resolution — in your portal.

q4.a: Verified profiles, booking-platform history, clear house rules, and deposits where appropriate. Bad fits are declined before they ever check in.

q5.q: Do you handle cleaning and laundry?
q5.a: Yes — dedicated housekeeping with hotel-grade turnover between every stay, photo-verified so nothing is missed.

q6.q: What about the pool and garden?
q6.a: Scheduled vendor visits, tracked like every other task — skimmed, tested, trimmed, and logged with photos.

q7.a: We guide you through local licensing and reporting requirements and keep the paperwork tracked — handled and documented, for complete peace of mind.

q1.q: Where will my villa be listed?
q1.a: Everywhere guests actually book: Airbnb, Booking.com, Expedia, Agoda, Vrbo, Trip.com, and direct through silqhaus.com — all synced in real time so double bookings can't happen.

q2.q: How do you price my nights?
q2.a: Dynamic pricing repriced every night against real demand, local events, and your true competitive set — data from PriceLabs and AirDNA, sharpened by our local judgment. Never guesswork.

q3.a: The operating system we built ourselves. It runs every property, task, booking, and payout in one place — the backbone that Mali, the staff app, and your owner portal plug into.

q4.q: What can I see in my owner portal?
q4.a: Your calendar, statements, documents, and every task on your home — updated in real time, open to you any hour, from anywhere.

q5.a: Our AI guest manager with a memory. Before every reply she reads the whole conversation, then checks your property's facts in our database — so guests get instant, correct answers in any language, at any hour.

q6.q: How do bookings stay in sync across platforms?
q6.a: Our PMS keeps every channel's calendar and rates aligned to the minute. One booking anywhere closes those dates everywhere.

q7.q: Why does the technology matter to me as an owner?
q7.a: Fewer mistakes, faster replies, and full transparency. Software carries the routine so our people can spend their time on what actually needs a human — your home and your guests.

metadata.title: Why Owners Choose Silqhaus | Property Management in Thailand
metadata.description: Built for year-round performance — not just high season. Discover why property owners trust Silqhaus for consistent quality control, real operational systems, and transparent numbers.

hero.subtitle: FOR PROPERTY OWNERS
hero.title: Why Owners Choose Silqhaus
hero.description: We are built for year-round performance — not just high season.

intro.title: Built for Every Season
intro.description: Most short-term rental operators only look good in peak season. Low season is where weak systems, weak teams, and weak processes get exposed.
intro.conclusion: Because a real business must survive all three.

hardTruth.subtitle: THE HARD TRUTH
hardTruth.title: Property Management is Operations — Not Marketing
hardTruth.description: Many property management companies invest heavily in social media, branding, and paid advertising. While visibility matters, it is not what determines whether your property earns consistent revenue.
points: Pretty posts, boosted ads, and "premium branding" do not protect your revenue.
If cleaning, maintenance, and guest communication are inconsistent, revenue will leak no matter how good the listings look.
Revenue protection comes from operational discipline — the systems behind the scenes that ensure every guest has a flawless experience.
At Silqhaus, marketing supports operations — not the other way around. We focus on building repeatable processes that deliver consistent results month after month.

selectivePortfolio.subtitle: QUALITY OVER QUANTITY
selectivePortfolio.title: Selective Portfolio = Real Quality Control
selectivePortfolio.description: We intentionally do not manage a large number of homes. Not because we cannot onboard more — but because we believe quality control is the single most important factor in long-term rental performance.
reasons: Quality control takes time — every unit requires dedicated attention to maintain standards
Regular checks and inspections catch issues before they reach guests
People matter — we train and retain our team rather than outsourcing to third parties
Accountability means one clear owner for every task, every property, every guest experience
selectivePortfolio.conclusion: We only onboard more properties when our technology and our team capacity scale first. Growth never comes at the cost of quality.

housekeeping.subtitle: IN-HOUSE OPERATIONS
housekeeping.title: In-House Housekeeping is Non-Negotiable
housekeeping.description: Housekeeping is the most visible part of property management to guests. It directly impacts reviews, repeat bookings, and your property's reputation. That is why we refuse to outsource it.

outsourcedProblems.title: Outsourced cleaning usually creates:
items: Inconsistent standards — different cleaners, different results every time
Slow problem resolution — finger-pointing between vendors and managers
Unclear responsibility — no single person accountable for cleanliness

ourModel.title: Our model:
items: In-house housekeeping team trained to hotel-grade standards
One unified standard across every property we manage
One clear owner of quality — our operations team, not a vendor

results.title: This gives:
items: Faster turnaround between guests with zero quality compromise
Consistent cleaning results that guests notice and mention in reviews
Real accountability — we know exactly who cleaned what and when

aiQuality.subtitle: AI-POWERED QUALITY CONTROL
aiQuality.title: Proof-Based Housekeeping Control
aiQuality.description: Trust is important, but proof is better. Silqhaus uses an internal AI-powered quality control system that removes guesswork from the cleaning process and gives property managers verifiable evidence of every turnover.
features: Housekeeping sends photo-based cleaning proof after every turnover
The AI system analyzes and tracks each unit's cleanliness performance over time
Property managers receive real, visual evidence for quality checks — not just verbal confirmation
Historical data reveals patterns, helping us improve and maintain consistently high standards

eliminates.title: This removes:
items: "I think it's clean" — replaced with photographic evidence
"The vendor said it was done" — replaced with verifiable, timestamped proof

aiQuality.conclusion: We operate with proof — not promises. Every clean is documented, every standard is measurable.

realTimeVisibility.subtitle: OWNER DASHBOARD
realTimeVisibility.title: Real-Time Visibility for Owners
realTimeVisibility.description: As a property owner, you should never feel disconnected from what's happening with your investment. Our owner dashboard gives you complete, real-time transparency into every aspect of your property's performance.
features: Real-time revenue tracking — see exactly what your property earns as bookings come in
Real-time booking activity — monitor upcoming reservations, check-ins, and check-outs
Real-time guest performance — track ratings, reviews, and guest satisfaction scores
Real-time payout records — every payment documented, every deduction explained
realTimeVisibility.conclusion: No waiting for monthly reports. No surprises. You always know exactly what is happening with your property.

payouts.subtitle: TRANSPARENT PAYOUTS
payouts.title: Faster and Clearer Owner Payout Logic
payouts.description: Financial transparency is not optional — it is foundational to a healthy owner-manager relationship. We designed our payout system so that owners never have to guess, ask, or wait to understand their earnings.
points: Each booking is visible — you see the guest, the dates, the rate, and the platform it came from.
Each payout is traceable — from booking confirmation to bank deposit, every step is documented.
Each deduction is transparent — maintenance costs, cleaning fees, commissions, and any other charges are itemized clearly.
Payouts are processed promptly — no waiting until end-of-quarter for your earnings.

assetProtection.subtitle: LONG-TERM THINKING
assetProtection.title: We Protect Your Home — Not Just Fill Your Calendar
assetProtection.description: Many operators prioritize maximum occupancy at any cost. We take a different approach. Your property is a long-term asset, and we treat it that way — balancing revenue generation with asset preservation.
goals: Stable, sustainable revenue that performs across all seasons — not just during peak months
Protected asset condition through regular maintenance, inspections, and preventive care
Controlled guest quality — we screen guests carefully to protect your home from damage and misuse
Long-term performance of your property — maintaining its value, condition, and earning potential for years to come

onboarding.subtitle: ONBOARDING PHILOSOPHY
onboarding.title: Onboarding is Part of Operations
onboarding.description: A successful rental property does not start with the first guest — it starts with proper preparation. Our onboarding process is designed to set your property up for long-term success from day one, addressing every operational detail before the first booking ever arrives.
steps: Pricing strategy — data-driven rate optimization based on market analysis and seasonal demand
Positioning — identifying your property's unique strengths and target guest profile
Listing structure — professional photography, compelling descriptions, and optimized platform presence
Operational workflows — check-in procedures, maintenance protocols, and emergency response plans
Housekeeping standards — detailed cleaning checklists customized to your property's specific needs
Guest communication flows — automated and personalized messaging from inquiry to post-checkout review

metadata.title: Our Story | Silqhaus — Thailand's First Decentralized Hotel Brand
metadata.description: A hotel that doesn't live in one building. Beachfront villas in Phuket, sky-rise suites in Pattaya — connected by one platform and run to one standard.

hero.title: Thailand's first decentralized hotel brand.
hero.alt: First light on the empty terrace of a Thai pool villa
hero.description: A hotel that doesn't live in one building. Silqhaus operates across Thailand's best coastlines and cities — beachfront villas in Phuket, sky-rise suites in Pattaya — all connected by one technology platform and run to one standard.

ourStory.statement: Different properties. Same experience. That's the idea.

beginning.title: The beginning.
beginning.p1: Silqhaus started with a question: why should a five-star experience require a five-star building?
beginning.p2: Our roots run deep in Thai real estate and hospitality. Years of working alongside property owners in Pattaya and Phuket showed us a gap on both sides of the market — owners with exceptional properties but no professional operation behind them, and travellers who wanted the space and privacy of a private home without giving up hotel standards.
beginning.p3: Silqhaus was built to close that gap.

timeline.title: Twelve months, in order.
timeline.intro: Everything below happened between July 2025 and today.

founded.title: Silqhaus begins, in Phuket
founded.desc: The company is founded and the first villas come under management. One destination, a handful of homes, and a rule we've kept since: never take on more than we can run properly.

pattaya.title: Pattaya opens
pattaya.desc: Three months in, a second coast — and the first real test of whether our standards travelled. They did.

licence.title: Licensed by the Tourism Authority
licence.desc: Tourism business licence No. 31/01480, issued 3 December — the paperwork a surprising number of operators here never bother with.

os.title: Silqhaus OS goes live
os.desc: Off-the-shelf property software was never built for the way we work, so we stopped renting it. Every booking, task, and payout has run through our own system since.

mali.title: Mali starts answering
mali.desc: Our AI guest manager goes live — reading the whole conversation and the property's own facts before every reply, in any language, at any hour.

today.title: Eleven homes, two destinations
today.desc: 1,256+ nights hosted and a 4.99★ average across every platform we list on.

quote.text: We didn't set out to build a management company. We set out to build the thing we wished existed when we were the ones handing over the keys.

decentralized.title: A hotel, decentralized.
decentralized.p1: A traditional hotel puts 200 identical rooms under one roof. We put ours where you actually want to stay.
decentralized.p2: Every Silqhaus property is different — that's the point. What never changes is the standard behind it. The same check-in experience. The same linen and cleanliness protocols. The same response time when you message us at midnight. Whether you're steps from the sand or thirty floors above the bay, you're staying at Silqhaus.

technology.title: Technology connects everything.
technology.p1: Behind every stay runs a single operating system. Dynamic pricing calibrated daily to the market. Guest communication answered around the clock. Housekeeping, maintenance, and quality checks tracked in real time across every property.
technology.p2: What a front desk does for one building, our technology does for an entire portfolio. That's how a decentralized brand keeps a centralized standard — and how our owners earn more while doing less.

philosophy.title: Our philosophy
philosophy.text: A place to stay should be the foundation of the memory, not just the backdrop. Every property in our portfolio is personally inspected and must meet our standards for quality, location, and guest experience. If we wouldn't stay there ourselves, it doesn't carry the Silqhaus name.

local.title: Local expertise
local.text: We don't manage Thailand from somewhere else — we live here. Hidden beach coves, the restaurants locals actually eat at, the right driver, the right tailor, the right time to visit the temple. Our team helps guests find the Thailand that exists beyond the tourist trail.

forward.title: Looking forward.
forward.p1: We believe travel is moving toward exactly what we've built: distributed, tech-enabled, locally rooted hospitality. More cities. More coastlines. One standard.
forward.p2: We're not just in the business of vacation rentals — we're building the hotel brand of the next decade, one property at a time.

cta.title: Come and see what we've built.
cta.description: Stay in one of our homes, or bring us yours.

phuket.metaDescription: Phuket beyond the beach — Old Town culture, Wat Chalong and the Big Buddha, Phang Nga Bay island days, spa rituals, photo spots, and the festivals worth planning around.
phuket.heroAlt: Aerial view of Phuket's west coast at golden hour, white sand and turquoise sea
phuket.stayLine: Staying in Phuket? Our villas are here.
phuket.highlightsIntro: Every beach below has its own full guide on our blog — written from living here, not from a press trip.
phuket.intro: Thailand's largest island is also its most complete — a pastel Sino-Portuguese old town, more than thirty beaches, island-studded seas in two directions, and some of the country's best spas. It's also home: our villas and our team live here. This is Phuket the way we'd show a friend.

culture.title: Culture — the island beyond the beach
culture.lead: Phuket's soul isn't on the sand. It's in the shophouse streets, the markets, and a heritage of tin-mining fortunes and Peranakan kitchens.

s1.name: Phuket Old Town
s1.desc: Pastel Sino-Portuguese shophouses along Thalang and Dibuk Roads — cafés, galleries, and some of Thailand's best-preserved streetscapes.

s2.name: Lard Yai Sunday market
s2.desc: Thalang Road closes to traffic on Sunday evenings — street food, local craft, and live music between the heritage facades.

s3.name: Kathu village
s3.desc: The island's tin-mining heartland — quiet temples, an old-town museum, and the origin story of Phuket's fortunes.

temples.title: Temples — from grand chedis to golden legends
temples.lead: Give the island one temple morning and it will repay you: go early, dress modestly, and take the hilltop light.

s1.name: Wat Chalong
s1.desc: Phuket's most revered temple — its Grand Pagoda is said to enshrine a fragment of the Buddha's bone.

s2.name: The Big Buddha
s2.desc: The 45-metre white marble Buddha on Nakkerd Hill — arrive for sunrise, before the coaches, when the whole island glows below.

s3.name: Wat Phra Thong
s3.desc: Thalang's half-buried golden Buddha, wrapped in three centuries of local legend.

islands.title: Islands — two seas to choose from
islands.lead: Phuket is a harbor as much as an island: limestone bays to the east, dive archipelagos to the north-west, and a boat for every mood.

s1.name: Phang Nga Bay
s1.desc: Limestone karsts, sea caves, and floating villages by longtail or kayak — James Bond Island is the postcard; Hong Island is the quieter frame.

s2.name: Phi Phi & Maya Bay
s2.desc: The famous one, and still worth it — go early in the day and early in the season.

s3.name: The Similan Islands
s3.desc: Granite boulders and gin-clear water north-west of Phuket — Thailand's benchmark diving, open October to May.

wellness.title: Wellness — the island that invented relaxing
wellness.lead: From a one-hour beach sala massage to a week-long resort ritual, Phuket takes recovery as seriously as adventure.

s1.name: Traditional Thai massage
s1.desc: From old-school shophouse studios in Phuket Town to salas right on the sand — the real thing costs a few hundred baht.

s2.name: Destination spas
s2.desc: World-class resort spas across the island's west coast — think ocean-facing pavilions at Trisara, Banyan Tree, and Amanpuri.

s3.name: Muay Thai & yoga camps
s3.desc: Train like a local in Chalong's gyms, or slow everything down at an island yoga shala.

photo.title: Photo tours — chasing the island's light
photo.lead: Phuket photographs best at its edges — first light on the hilltops, last light on the capes, blue hour in the old town.

s1.name: Promthep Cape
s1.desc: The island's southern tip and its definitive sunset — arrive an hour early for a spot on the rail.

s2.name: Karon Viewpoint
s2.desc: Three bays — Kata Noi, Kata, and Karon — stacked in a single frame.

s3.name: Old Town at blue hour
s3.desc: Neon signs warming up against pastel facades — Thalang Road is the classic frame.

festivals.title: Festivals — when the island celebrates
festivals.lead: Time a trip to one of these and Phuket becomes a different island entirely.

s1.name: Songkran · April
s1.desc: Thai New Year — three days when the whole island becomes a joyful water fight.

s2.name: Vegetarian Festival · Sep–Oct
s2.desc: Nine days of processions, drums, and firecrackers — Phuket's most intense and most local tradition.

s3.name: Loy Krathong · November
s3.desc: Candlelit krathongs released on every beach and lagoon — the island's gentlest night of the year.

areas.title: Know your side of the island.
areas.intro: Phuket changes character every few kilometres — west coast for sunsets, east coast for calm water, and a green middle most visitors never see.
areas.hint: Hover an area to find it on the map

phuketTown.name: Phuket Town (Old Town)
phuketTown.desc: Pastel Sino-Portuguese shophouses, Peranakan kitchens, and the island's only real streetlife after dark — the antidote to the beach strips.

patong.name: Patong
patong.desc: The island's loudest room — Bangla Road, jet skis, and every holiday service imaginable packed into two square kilometres.

karon.name: Karon
karon.desc: Patong with the volume down two notches — a long straight beach, squeaky white sand, and room to breathe.

kata.name: Kata & Kata Noi
kata.desc: Surf schools in low season, families in high — with Kata Noi around the headland, quieter and prettier still.

naiHarn.name: Nai Harn
naiHarn.desc: The local favourite at the southern tip — a lagoon behind, a near-perfect bay in front, and not a high-rise in sight.

rawai.name: Rawai & Chalong
rawai.desc: Where Phuket actually lives — longtail piers, seafood by the kilo, and the launch point for every island day.

kamala.name: Kamala
kamala.desc: Millionaire's Mile on the headland, a quiet Muslim fishing village on the sand — the island's most surprising split personality.

surin.name: Surin
surin.desc: Old-money Phuket — beach clubs under casuarina trees and villas tucked up the hillside, out of view.

bangTao.name: Bang Tao & Laguna
bangTao.desc: Six kilometres of sand fronting the resort belt, with Boat Avenue's restaurants and Friday market just inland.

naithon.name: Nai Thon & Layan
naithon.desc: The quiet north-west — one low-rise row behind the beach and almost no through traffic.

naiYang.name: Nai Yang & Mai Khao
naiYang.desc: National-park sand under casuarina shade, and a runway close enough to watch the landings from the water.

capePanwa.name: Cape Panwa
capePanwa.desc: The east-coast headland — aquarium, deep-water piers, and the sunrises the west coast never gets.

thalang.name: Thalang & the interior
thalang.desc: The green middle — waterfalls, rubber plantations, the Heroines Monument, and Phuket before tourism arrived.

practical.title: Getting around, shopping & good to know.
practical.lead: The practical side of the island, in three parts — open a section to dive in.

transport.title: Getting there & around.
transport.lead: There's no train and no meter — Phuket runs on rental cars, scooters, and whichever pier you leave from.

airport.name: One airport, up north
airport.desc: Phuket International (HKT) sits at the island's top end — allow 40 minutes down to Bang Tao, and up to 90 to Patong in traffic.

car.name: Rent a car
car.desc: The island is bigger than it looks and the hills are real — a car is the difference between three beaches in a day and one.

ride.name: Grab, Bolt & taxis
ride.desc: App rides now cover most of the island and settle the old taxi arguments — coverage thins after midnight and out in Thalang.

moto.name: Scooters
moto.desc: The local default and the local hazard — helmet on, licence in the wallet, and stay off the Patong hill in the rain.

bus.name: Songthaews & smart buses
bus.desc: Blue songthaews run beach-to-town on fixed routes for pocket change; the airport smart bus is the cheapest way in.

ferry.name: Piers & island boats
ferry.desc: Rassada for Phi Phi and Krabi, Chalong for day trips, Bang Rong for Koh Yao — pick the pier before you book the boat.

shopping.title: Shopping — markets first, malls second.
shopping.lead: Phuket shops in three registers: air-conditioned malls out on the bypass, weekend markets worth planning around, and night bazaars that only wake at seven.

s1.name: Central Phuket
s1.desc: Floresta and Festival joined at the hip on the bypass — the island's only full-scale mall day.

s2.name: Jungceylon
s2.desc: Patong's indoor escape — practical rather than glamorous, and very welcome when the sun is brutal.

s3.name: Central Village
s3.desc: The outlet mall near the airport — last-day bargain territory if your flight is an evening one.

s1.name: Naka Weekend Market
s1.desc: The big Saturday–Sunday sprawl below Central — clothes, phone cases, and a serious food alley.

s2.name: Lard Yai walking street
s2.desc: Thalang Road closed to cars on Sundays — the island's most atmospheric market, heritage facades and all.

s3.name: Banzaan Fresh Market
s3.desc: Patong's proper wet market behind Jungceylon — buy the fish downstairs, have it cooked upstairs.

s1.name: Chillva Market
s1.desc: Phuket Town's container-yard night market — where the island's twenty-somethings actually go.

s2.name: Boat Avenue & Porto de Phuket
s2.desc: Cherngtalay's restaurant strip, with a Friday market that pulls in the whole north-west coast.

s3.name: Malin Plaza
s3.desc: Patong's open-air food court near the sea — grilled seafood, cold beer, no pretence.

good.title: Good to know
good.lead: The small things that make Phuket easier.

sim.name: Get a Thai eSIM on arrival
sim.desc: Data from the moment you land — you'll want it for Grab, maps, and checking the ferry timetables.

cash.name: Cash for markets, cards for malls
cash.desc: Beach vendors, songthaews, and longtail boatmen want baht; malls, resorts, and Grab take cards. Keep small notes.

temple.name: Cover shoulders and knees
temple.desc: Wat Chalong and the Big Buddha enforce it — carry a light layer, and slip your shoes off where the signs ask.

riptide.name: Respect the red flags
riptide.desc: The west coast gets serious rip currents from May to October. A red flag means out of the water — every year people ignore it.

scooter.name: Helmet, licence, no flip-flops
scooter.desc: Checkpoints are routine, and most travel insurance voids without a motorcycle licence. The hills punish inexperience.

season.name: Know which month, which coast
season.desc: November to April is the postcard; May to October brings rain, swell, and half-price villas — the east coast stays calmer either way.

things.title: Thirty things to do in Phuket.
things.lead: The island checklist — tick them off across a long weekend, a low season, or a life lived here.

items.i1: Watch the sun drop off Promthep Cape with everyone else, and not mind
items.i2: Climb to the Big Buddha for the island's widest view
items.i3: Pay respects at Wat Chalong, Phuket's most revered temple
items.i4: Wander Old Town's pastel shophouses along Thalang and Dibuk Roads
items.i5: Eat your way down Lard Yai on a Sunday evening
items.i6: Take a longtail through Phang Nga Bay's limestone karsts
items.i7: Kayak into the hongs — the collapsed caves hidden inside the islands
items.i8: Reach Coral Island early and swim before the tour boats land
items.i9: Sail to the Similans for the clearest water in Thailand (Oct–May)
items.i10: Snorkel Racha Yai's shallow reef on a calm morning
items.i11: Learn to surf on Kata's low-season break
items.i12: Drive the Karon viewpoint road for the three-bay panorama
items.i13: Swim at Freedom Beach after the longtail drops you off
items.i14: Find Ya Nui's tiny cove below the windmill
items.i15: Watch the planes come in low over Mai Khao from the sand
items.i16: Book a proper Thai massage, then a proper spa day
items.i17: Eat Hokkien mee in an Old Town coffee shop that predates you
items.i18: Try Peranakan cooking — the island's own Sino-Thai kitchen
items.i19: Buy the day's catch at Rawai seafood market and have it grilled
items.i20: Take a cooking class and learn southern curries, not Bangkok ones
items.i21: Drink a sundowner at a Surin or Kamala beach club
items.i22: See a Muay Thai fight at a Patong stadium
items.i23: Walk Bangla Road once, for the anthropology
items.i24: Cross to Koh Yao Noi for the Phuket that stopped in 1995
items.i25: Ride out to Bang Pae and Ton Sai waterfalls after the rain
items.i26: Visit the Phuket Elephant Sanctuary — retired elephants, no riding
items.i27: Catch the Vegetarian Festival's processions in September or October
items.i28: Walk up Khao Rang for a town-side sunset instead of a beach one
items.i29: Get out to Sirinat National Park for empty northern sand
items.i30: Ferry to Phi Phi and stay the night, after the day boats leave

pattaya.intro: Pattaya gets typecast, and it shouldn't be. Two hours from Bangkok, our second home is a bay of quiet northern sands, a temple carved entirely from teak, islands you can reach by longtail — and one of Thailand's best city sunsets from Pratumnak Hill. Here's the Pattaya we actually live in.

culture.title: Culture — more than the postcard
culture.lead: Between the beach crowds lives a Pattaya of hand-carved teak, floating kitchens, and market nights.

s1.name: The Sanctuary of Truth
s1.desc: A 105-metre temple carved entirely from teak — no nails, all myth. Come at golden hour, when the seafront spires catch fire.

s2.name: Pattaya Floating Market
s2.desc: Four regions of Thailand trading from one lake — food first, crafts second, boat-to-boat.

s3.name: Thepprasit Night Market
s3.desc: Pattaya's biggest night market — come hungry, leave with souvenirs you didn't plan on.

temples.title: Temples — hilltop, cliff-face, and royal
temples.lead: Pattaya's sacred sites come supersized, and each earns its detour.

s1.name: Wat Phra Yai (Big Buddha Hill)
s1.desc: The 18-metre golden Buddha that has watched over the bay from Pratumnak Hill since 1940.

s2.name: Khao Chi Chan
s2.desc: A 109-metre Buddha traced in gold on a sheer limestone cliff — clearest light in the morning.

s3.name: Wat Yansangwararam
s3.desc: A serene royal temple complex twenty minutes south, gardens and lake included.

islands.title: Islands — turquoise within sight of the skyline
islands.lead: The gulf's near islands are Pattaya's best-kept secret: white sand a short boat ride from your villa.

s1.name: Koh Larn
s1.desc: The Coral Island — 45 minutes by ferry or 15 by speedboat. Tawaen Beach for the buzz, Samae for the calm.

s2.name: Koh Sak
s2.desc: A quiet horseshoe of sand just past Koh Larn — snorkeling and not much else, blissfully.

s3.name: Koh Phai
s3.desc: The furthest of the near islands — navy-kept, day-trip only, and the clearest water in the bay.

wellness.title: Wellness — the bay at its quietest
wellness.lead: Between beach days, Pattaya restores as well as it entertains.

s1.name: Oceanfront spas
s1.desc: Resort spas on Wongamat and Pratumnak — treatments with the gulf as the soundtrack.

s2.name: Thai massage on Jomtien
s2.desc: Beachside salas and old-school studios by the kilometre — the real thing, a few hundred baht.

s3.name: Muay Thai gyms
s3.desc: Train alongside fighters at gyms from Naklua down to Jomtien.

photo.title: Photo tours — a city on a crescent bay
photo.lead: Pattaya photographs far better than it gets credit for — especially at the edges of the day.

s1.name: Khao Pattaya Viewpoint
s1.desc: The classic crescent-bay frame from Pratumnak Hill — best at blue hour as the city lights come on.

s2.name: Sanctuary of Truth at sunset
s2.desc: Carved spires against a burning sky — shoot from the seawall below.

s3.name: Wongamat sunset
s3.desc: Naklua's quiet sand faces west — longtails, gulls, and a low golden sun.

festivals.title: Festivals — the loudest parties, the gentlest nights
festivals.lead: Time a trip to one of these and Pattaya becomes a different city entirely.

s1.name: Wan Lai Songkran · 18–19 April
s1.desc: Pattaya celebrates Thai New Year a week late and twice as wet — Beach Road becomes a water parade.

s2.name: International Fireworks Festival · November
s2.desc: Two nights of world-class pyrotechnics over the bay — book a sea-view balcony early.

s3.name: Loy Krathong · November
s3.desc: Candlelit krathongs drifting from Jomtien to Naklua — the whole bay glitters.

areas.title: Know your stretch of the coast.
areas.intro: One bay, many personalities — Pattaya changes completely every couple of kilometres down the coast road, so pick your stretch first.
areas.hint: Hover an area to find it on the map

naklua.name: Naklua & Wongamat
naklua.desc: The quiet money end — the best in-town sand, sunset beach clubs, and the Sanctuary of Truth on the headland. Our home beach.

central.name: Central Pattaya & Beach Road
central.desc: The promenade heart — malls, the new beach clubs, and every baht-bus route. Locals stroll the sand here and swim elsewhere.

walkingStreet.name: South Pattaya & Walking Street
walkingStreet.desc: The neon legend, pedestrian-only after seven — louder than ever, more pan-Asian than its reputation, and the pier for Koh Larn boats.

pratumnak.name: Pratumnak Hill & Cozy Beach
pratumnak.desc: The green hill between the bays — viewpoints, the Big Buddha, and a village-quiet feel ten minutes from everything.

jomtien.name: Jomtien & Dongtan
jomtien.desc: The long family beach with a freshly rebuilt promenade — and tree-shaded, jet-ski-free Dongtan at its calmest end.

naJomtien.name: Na Jomtien & Ocean Marina
naJomtien.desc: Pattaya's quiet-luxury strip — genuinely swimmable water, Southeast Asia's largest marina, and the newest five-star flags.

bangsaray.name: Bangsaray
bangsaray.desc: A real fishing village twenty-five minutes south — near-empty weekday sand and stilted seafood restaurants over the water.

eastPattaya.name: East Pattaya & Lake Mabprachan
eastPattaya.desc: Pool-villa country inland — the lake loop, the golf courses, and the space families actually live in.

kohLarn.name: Koh Larn
kohLarn.desc: The island escape, forty baht and forty minutes away — busy Tawaen, quieter Samae, and clear water the mainland can't match.

practical.title: Getting around, shopping & good to know.
practical.lead: The practical side of the bay, in three parts — open a section to dive in.

transport.title: Getting there & around.
transport.lead: No trains and no meters — Pattaya runs on the motorway, the baht bus, and the boats from Bali Hai Pier.

fromBangkok.name: From Bangkok by road
fromBangkok.desc: Two hours down Motorway 7 — a private transfer for ease, or the Ekkamai bus every half hour for 148 baht. The fast train remains a rumour.

airport.name: U-Tapao, the small airport
airport.desc: Forty-five minutes south with a thin flight list — most guests fly into Bangkok and drive down. Its big expansion won't change that before 2030.

bahtBus.name: The baht bus
bahtBus.desc: Pattaya's icon — hop on the back, ride the loop, press the buzzer, pay 15 baht as you step off. Board silently, or you may accidentally charter one.

ride.name: Grab, Bolt & friends
ride.desc: All the apps work here — 60–150 baht across town, honest prices at night, and cards settle in-app.

moto.name: Motorcycle taxis
moto.desc: Orange vests at every soi mouth — agree the fare first near the tourist strips, or just book a GrabBike.

ferry.name: Boats to Koh Larn
ferry.desc: The 40-baht public ferry from Bali Hai's new floating piers, forty minutes each way — last boats back run five to six depending on the pier, or it's a speedboat fare home.

shopping.title: Shopping — malls by day, markets by night.
shopping.lead: Pattaya shops in three registers: a flagship mall row, seafood-and-produce markets, and night bazaars that just keep opening.

s1.name: Terminal 21
s1.desc: The airport-themed flagship — 500 shops across six themed floors, and the famously cheap Pier 21 food court.

s2.name: Central Pattaya
s2.desc: The beachfront giant under the Hilton — everyone still calls it Central Festival, and everyone still meets there.

s3.name: Central Marina Outlet
s3.desc: North Pattaya's day-to-night outlet mall — brand discounts inside, a night market out front until late.

s1.name: Thepprasit Night Market
s1.desc: The big one on the Jomtien side — open nightly now, but Friday to Sunday brings the full food-and-everything sprawl.

s2.name: Lan Pho Naklua
s2.desc: Naklua's seafood market, rebuilt in 2025 — fresh off the boats, minutes from Wongamat.

s3.name: Tree Town
s3.desc: Soi Buakhao's produce market by day, open-air bar-and-grill sprawl by night — where the town's regulars end their evenings.

s1.name: Yai Mak Market
s1.desc: Jomtien's newest and now largest night market — food stalls, courtyard bars, and live-music stages.

s2.name: Runway Street Food
s2.desc: Street food under a full-size jumbo jet on Second Road — as photogenic as dinner gets.

s3.name: Jomtien Night Market
s3.desc: The nightly food-court-and-dance-floor institution — family crowds, and pelmeni next to the pad thai.

good.title: Good to know
good.lead: The small things that make Pattaya easier.

sim.name: Get a Thai eSIM on arrival
sim.desc: Data the moment you land — you'll want it for Grab, maps, and checking which day the water parks close.

cash.name: Cash for the baht bus, cards for the malls
cash.desc: Baht buses, ferries, markets, and beach vendors want small notes; malls, resorts, and Grab take cards. Thai ATMs charge 220 baht a withdrawal — take out plenty.

temple.name: Cover shoulders and knees
temple.desc: The Sanctuary of Truth lends sarongs and the Big Buddha expects respect — carry a light layer, shoes off where the signs ask.

jetski.name: Skip the beachfront jet-skis
jetski.desc: The damage-claim scam is Pattaya's oldest trick. If you must, video the machine with the operator in frame first — and the Tourist Police answer on 1155.

wednesday.name: Beware the Wednesday rule
wednesday.desc: Both big water parks close on Wednesdays, and the city's chair-free beach-cleaning days tend to land on one too — check before you plan the day around either.

season.name: Know your season
season.desc: November to February is the postcard; May to October brings short, hard afternoon bursts — though this coast stays drier than the Andaman in the same months.

things.title: Thirty things to do in Pattaya.
things.lead: The bay checklist — tick them off across a weekend, a season, or the years this coast keeps pulling you back.

items.i1: Put on a hard hat and watch the carvers at work inside the Sanctuary of Truth — all teak, no nails
items.i2: Take an early boat to Koh Larn and claim Samae Beach before the speedboats land
items.i3: Climb the naga staircase to the Big Buddha on Pratumnak Hill
items.i4: Stand beneath Khao Chi Chan's 109-metre laser-carved Buddha
items.i5: Toast the sunset at a Wongamat beach club, ten minutes from the villa
items.i6: Pick your dinner from the boats at the rebuilt Lan Pho Naklua seafood market
items.i7: Ride a baht bus around the full Beach Road loop for 15 baht
items.i8: Walk Walking Street once, for the neon anthropology
items.i9: Pick a side in the great cabaret debate: Tiffany's or Alcazar
items.i10: Take a ringside seat at Max Muay Thai — fights every night of the year
items.i11: Lose a day on Ramayana's 26 slides — Thailand's biggest water park
items.i12: Do the movie-lot version at Columbia Pictures Aquaverse
items.i13: Watch the whole bay curve below Khao Pattaya Viewpoint at dusk
items.i14: Wander the French parterre and the dinosaur valley at Nong Nooch
items.i15: Say hello to the hippos of Khao Kheow Open Zoo — Moo Deng's home turf
items.i16: Drive the Route 331 loop: Buddha Mountain, Silverlake Vineyard, Wat Yan
items.i17: Sit a quiet hour at Wat Yansangwararam, the royal monastery in a garden
items.i18: Feed rescued elephants at a saddle-off sanctuary — no riding, no shows
items.i19: Graze your way through Thepprasit Night Market on a Friday or Saturday
items.i20: Find the street-food market under a full-size jumbo jet at Runway
items.i21: Book the cliff-edge table at Rimpa Lapin above Bangsaray
items.i22: Spend a slow morning on Bangsaray's fishing-village sand
items.i23: Eat at one of Pattaya's Michelin Bib Gourmand kitchens
items.i24: Go full Ibiza — pool, DJs, and sunset at Café del Mar Na Jomtien
items.i25: Walk Jomtien's brand-new promenade as the lights come on
items.i26: Claim a tree-shaded, jet-ski-free stretch of Dongtan Beach
items.i27: Time a November trip to the International Fireworks Festival
items.i28: Join the Wan Lai water fight when Songkran reaches Pattaya (18–19 April)
items.i29: Go bohemian at Wonderfruit in December — music, art, and open fields
items.i30: Stay on Koh Larn past the last ferry, when the island exhales

bangkok.metaDescription: Bangkok the way locals live it — the Grand Palace and Wat Arun, Chinatown after dark, river islands and the Green Lung, rooftop sunsets, and the festivals that stop the city.
bangkok.heroAlt: Bangkok at dusk with the Chao Phraya river curving through the lit skyline
bangkok.stayLine: After Bangkok? Our villas are in Phuket & Pattaya.
bangkok.intro: Every Thailand trip starts here whether you plan it or not — so plan it. Give Bangkok three days and it repays you in gold-spired temples, river islands, rooftop sunsets, and the best street food on the planet. This is the capital as we actually eat, walk, and photograph it.

areas.title: Know your neighborhoods.
areas.intro: Bangkok is a city of villages wearing a metropolis costume — pick the right base and the city opens up.
areas.hint: Hover a neighborhood to find it on the map

rattanakosin.name: Rattanakosin (Old Town)
rattanakosin.desc: The royal island of the Grand Palace, Wat Pho, and the amulet markets — Bangkok's ceremonial heart.

riverside.name: Riverside (Charoenkrung–Bang Rak)
riverside.desc: The old trading riverfront turned creative district — heritage hotels, Warehouse 30, and ICONSIAM glittering across the water.

yaowarat.name: Yaowarat & Songwat
yaowarat.desc: Chinatown's neon food mile — and Songwat, its riverside backstreet where old godowns are now cafés and galleries.

khaosan.name: Khao San & Banglamphu
khaosan.desc: The backpacker legend, aging gracefully — come for the buzz, stay for old Banglamphu's shophouse kitchens.

siam.name: Siam & Ratchaprasong
siam.desc: The retail nucleus — mega-malls chained together by skywalks, with the Erawan Shrine steps from the designer flagships.

silomSathorn.name: Silom & Sathorn
silomSathorn.desc: The financial district that moonlights as a nightlife district — Lumpini Park mornings, rooftop bars at dusk.

sukhumvit.name: Sukhumvit (Asok–Phrom Phong)
sukhumvit.desc: The cosmopolitan artery — Japanese enclaves, the EM District malls, and side-soi restaurants that reward wandering.

thonglor.name: Thonglor & Ekkamai
thonglor.desc: Bangkok's coolest kids — natural-wine bars, izakayas, specialty coffee, and design shops down every soi.

ari.name: Ari
ari.desc: The leafy local favorite — brunch cafés and slow sois, fifteen minutes from Chatuchak on the BTS.

ratchada.name: Ratchada & Huai Khwang
ratchada.desc: Night-market territory along the MRT, with late-night Chinese-Thai kitchens that never seem to close.

dusit.name: Dusit
dusit.desc: The royal quarter — the Marble Temple, Ananta Samakhom's dome, and Bangkok at its most stately.

chatuchakArea.name: Chatuchak
chatuchakArea.desc: Weekend-market country — 15,000 stalls, Or Tor Kor's gourmet produce, and two big green parks.

phraKhanong.name: Phra Khanong & On Nut
phraKhanong.desc: Sukhumvit's next chapter — night markets, craft-beer bars, and rents the creative crowd can still afford.

bangKrachao.name: Bang Krachao
bangKrachao.desc: The Green Lung — a jungle island in the river's bend, twenty minutes and a world away.

practical.title: Getting around, shopping & good to know.
practical.lead: The practical side of the capital, in three parts — open a section to dive in.

good.title: Good to know
good.lead: The small things that make Bangkok easier.

sim.name: Get a Thai eSIM on arrival
sim.desc: Data the moment you land — cheaper and simpler than a SIM counter, and you'll want it for Grab and maps.

cash.name: Cash for markets, cards for malls
cash.desc: Street stalls, taxis, and tuk-tuks want baht; malls, hotels, and Grab take cards. Keep small notes handy.

temple.name: Cover shoulders and knees
temple.desc: Temples enforce it — carry a light layer, and slip your shoes off where the signs ask.

tuktuk.name: Agree the fare first
tuktuk.desc: Tuk-tuks and some taxis won't meter for tourists — settle the price before you climb in, or just use Grab.

water.name: Drink bottled water
water.desc: Tap water isn't for drinking; bottled is everywhere and cheap. Pace yourself in the afternoon heat.

shopping.title: Shopping — a national sport.
shopping.lead: Bangkok shops in three registers: ice-cold mega-malls, sprawling markets, and night bazaars — most visits need all three.

s1.name: Siam Paragon & Siam Center
s1.desc: The flagship cluster at the BTS's crossroads — luxury below, food halls above.

s2.name: ICONSIAM
s2.desc: The riverside giant with an indoor floating market — worth the crossing for the building alone.

s3.name: The EM District
s3.desc: EmQuartier, Emporium, and Emsphere stacked along Phrom Phong — Sukhumvit's polished heart.

s1.name: Chatuchak
s1.desc: The weekend giant — 15,000 stalls, from vintage denim to garden orchids.

s2.name: Pratunam & Platinum
s2.desc: Wholesale fashion by the rack — where half of Southeast Asia stocks its boutiques.

s3.name: Sampeng Lane
s3.desc: Chinatown's ribbon of haberdashery chaos — fabric, beads, and everything by the dozen.

s1.name: Talad Rot Fai Srinakarin
s1.desc: The vintage night market — classic cars, retro barbers, and smoke rising off a hundred grills.

s2.name: Warehouse 30 & Charoenkrung
s2.desc: The creative district's design shops, galleries, and coffee in converted river godowns.

s3.name: Asiatique
s3.desc: The riverside night bazaar — a ferris wheel, open-air dining, and easy souvenir sweeps.

things.title: Thirty things to do in Bangkok.
things.lead: The capital checklist — tick them off across a first trip, a fifth, or a lifetime.

items.i1: Watch dawn hit the Grand Palace before the crowds do
items.i2: Meet the Emerald Buddha at Wat Phra Kaew
items.i3: Stand at the feet of Wat Pho's Reclining Buddha
items.i4: Cross the river and climb Wat Arun
items.i5: Circle the Golden Mount at dusk
items.i6: Find the 37 spires of Loha Prasat, the Metal Castle
items.i7: Take the Marble Temple on a quiet morning
items.i8: Pay respects at the City Pillar Shrine
items.i9: Eat your way down Yaowarat after dark
items.i10: Stack the little bowls at a boat-noodle alley
items.i11: Cook Thai for a morning, market run included
items.i12: Graze the gourmet stalls of Or Tor Kor market
items.i13: Hunt vintage treasure through Chatuchak's 15,000 stalls
items.i14: Smell the marigolds at the midnight flower market
items.i15: Decode Thainess at the Museum of Siam
items.i16: See what Thai artists are making at MOCA
items.i17: Walk the royal halls of the National Museum
items.i18: Cycle the jungle paths of Bang Krachao, the Green Lung
items.i19: Ride a longtail through the Thonburi canals
items.i20: Catch a puppet show at the Artist's House
items.i21: Ferry to Koh Kret for pottery and river breeze
items.i22: Day-trip to the island city of Ayutthaya
items.i23: Learn massage where it was invented, at Wat Pho
items.i24: Sweat through one honest Muay Thai class
items.i25: Join the six a.m. tai chi circles in Lumpini Park
items.i26: Book a spa afternoon high above the skyline
items.i27: Toast the sunset from a rooftop bar
items.i28: Shoot Wat Arun at blue hour from Tha Tien pier
items.i29: Wander Talat Noi's painted alleys and old engines
items.i30: Ride the Chao Phraya Express at golden hour, just because

transport.title: Getting there & around.
transport.lead: Bangkok traffic is legendary — but the rails, the river, and the motorbike sois beat it daily.

airports.name: Two airports
airports.desc: Suvarnabhumi (BKK) for full-service airlines, Don Mueang (DMK) for budget carriers — check which one is on your ticket, twice.

airportRail.name: Airport Rail Link
airportRail.desc: Suvarnabhumi to the city in about 26 minutes, connecting to the BTS at Phaya Thai.

rail.name: BTS Skytrain & MRT
rail.desc: Fast, cold, and rush-hour packed — the modern city runs on them. Grab a stored-value card on day one.

river.name: River & canal boats
river.desc: The Chao Phraya Express and Saen Saep canal line — the fastest way across old Bangkok, and the most scenic.

ride.name: Grab, taxis & tuk-tuks
ride.desc: Grab for honesty, meter taxis for luck, tuk-tuks for the story — agree the price before you sit down.

moto.name: Motorcycle taxis
moto.desc: Orange vests at every soi mouth — the rush-hour cheat code for short hops.

culture.title: Culture — a city of layers
culture.lead: Bangkok stacks royal splendor over canal-side life over 24-hour markets — give each layer its own day.

s1.name: The Grand Palace & Wat Phra Kaew
s1.desc: Thailand's most sacred ground — the Emerald Buddha and gold at every turn. Arrive at opening, shoulders covered.

s2.name: Chinatown (Yaowarat)
s2.desc: Neon, gold shops, and the city's densest food street after dark — come hungry and follow the queues.

s3.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
s3.desc: Fifteen thousand stalls of everything imaginable — go early, and let your nose navigate.

s4.name: Museum of Siam
s4.desc: The interactive 'discovery museum' that decodes what it means to be Thai — if you visit one museum, make it this.

s5.name: Pak Khlong Talad
s5.desc: The flower market that never closes — go toward midnight, when the marigold trucks unload.

s6.name: A Thai cooking class
s6.desc: From market basket to plate in a morning — the souvenir you'll actually use forever.

temples.title: Temples — gold at every turn
temples.lead: The capital's wats range from imperial to intimate — these cover the spectrum.

s1.name: Wat Arun
s1.desc: The Temple of Dawn, studded with porcelain — climb it at noon, admire it from the opposite bank at sunset.

s2.name: Wat Pho
s2.desc: The 46-metre Reclining Buddha — and the birthplace of Thai massage. Get one on the premises.

s3.name: Wat Benchamabophit
s3.desc: The Marble Temple — Carrara stone drawn in Thai lines, and a fraction of the crowds.

s4.name: Wat Saket (the Golden Mount)
s4.desc: Three hundred steps spiral up to the gilded chedi — old Bangkok's best panorama, softest at dusk.

s5.name: Loha Prasat
s5.desc: The 37-spired 'Metal Castle' at Wat Ratchanadda — one of the last of its kind on earth, and strangely serene.

islands.title: Islands — yes, Bangkok has them
islands.lead: The Chao Phraya hides green escapes minutes from the skyline — and Thailand's old capital is an island too.

s1.name: Bang Krachao
s1.desc: The 'Green Lung' — a jungle island in a bend of the river, best explored by bicycle on raised paths.

s2.name: Koh Kret
s2.desc: A car-free pottery island upriver — Mon communities, river breeze, and a lively Sunday market.

s3.name: Ayutthaya
s3.desc: The old capital literally is an island — three rivers around four centuries of ruins, an easy day trip north.

s4.name: The Thonburi khlongs
s4.desc: A longtail through the west bank's canals — stilt houses, temple piers, and the Artist's House puppet theatre. Bangkok as Venice, one hour.

wellness.title: Wellness — the original urban retreat
wellness.lead: Bangkok invented recovering from Bangkok — from massage's birthplace to spas above the clouds.

s1.name: Wat Pho Massage School
s1.desc: Learn — or simply receive — Thai massage where it was first codified.

s2.name: Sky-high hotel spas
s2.desc: World-ranked spas at The Peninsula, Mandarin Oriental, and Banyan Tree — treatments with the skyline underfoot.

s3.name: Lumpini Park at dawn
s3.desc: Tai chi circles, monitor lizards, and the softest light the city gets — six a.m. is the secret.

photo.title: Photo tours — the city of golden hours
photo.lead: Bangkok photographs in layers: river, rooftop, and backstreet each keep their own light.

s1.name: Wat Arun from Tha Tien
s1.desc: The cross-river blue-hour classic — spires lighting up as long-tail boats streak the frame.

s2.name: Rooftop sunsets
s2.desc: The sprawl going amber from Mahanakhon SkyWalk or a riverside rooftop bar.

s3.name: Talat Noi
s3.desc: Street art, old Chinese shophouses, and vintage engine parts — Bangkok's most photogenic backstreets.

festivals.title: Festivals — the capital celebrates hardest
festivals.lead: When Bangkok celebrates, whole districts transform — time your trip to one of these.

s1.name: Songkran · April
s1.desc: Silom and Khao San become joyful water battlefields; the temples keep the gentler rituals.

s2.name: Loy Krathong · November
s2.desc: Krathongs on the Chao Phraya and every park lake — the river glows from Asiatique to Rama VIII.

s3.name: Chinese New Year · Jan–Feb
s3.desc: Yaowarat erupts — lion dances, red lanterns, and food stalls to the horizon.

cool.title: Cool Season (November - February)
cool.description: Ideal weather with comfortable temperatures (70-85°F) and minimal rainfall. Perfect for sightseeing, outdoor activities, and beach vacations. Peak tourist season with higher prices.

hot.title: Hot Season (March - May)
hot.description: Hot and humid with temperatures reaching 95°F+. Excellent for beach destinations and swimming. Fewer crowds and competitive accommodation rates.

rainy.title: Rainy Season (June - October)
rainy.description: Monsoon season with afternoon showers and high humidity. Lush landscapes, lowest prices, and fewer tourists. Great for cultural experiences and indoor activities.

phuket.title: Phuket
phuket.subtitle: Thailand’s largest island, where turquoise waters meet lush tropical landscapes and world-class luxury
phuket.discoverP1: Thailand’s largest island, Phuket is a tropical paradise that offers the perfect blend of natural beauty, cultural richness, and modern luxury. From the vibrant nightlife of Patong to the serene beaches of Kata and Karon, Phuket caters to every type of traveler.
phuket.discoverP2: The island’s west coast is lined with stunning beaches, each with its own character—from the bustling shores of Patong to the peaceful coves of Nai Harn. Inland, you’ll discover lush rainforests, hidden waterfalls, and the iconic Big Buddha overlooking the island.
phuket.discoverP3: Our curated collection of luxury villas in Phuket provides the ultimate base for exploring this stunning destination. Wake up to panoramic ocean views, enjoy private infinity pools overlooking the Andaman Sea, and experience Thai hospitality at its finest.
phuket.attractionsSubtitle: Explore the best attractions Phuket has to offer

patongBeach.name: Patong Beach
patongBeach.description: The most famous and vibrant beach in Phuket, Patong is the heart of the island’s entertainment scene. This 3-kilometer stretch of sand offers crystal-clear waters perfect for swimming and water sports. By day, enjoy jet skiing, parasailing, and beach volleyball. By night, the beachfront comes alive with restaurants, bars, and clubs.

kataBeach.name: Kata Beach
kataBeach.description: Kata Beach is divided into two bays - Kata Yai (Big Kata) and Kata Noi (Little Kata). This family-friendly destination offers calm, clear waters ideal for swimming and snorkeling. The beach is particularly popular with surfers during the monsoon season when waves can reach impressive heights.

yaNuiBeach.name: Ya Nui Beach
yaNuiBeach.description: A hidden gem tucked between rocky headlands, Ya Nui Beach is a small, secluded spot perfect for snorkeling and kayaking. The calm waters are home to vibrant coral reefs and abundant marine life, making it a favorite among nature lovers.

maiKhaoBeach.name: Mai Khao Beach
maiKhaoBeach.description: Stretching over 11 kilometers, Mai Khao is Phuket’s longest beach and part of Sirinat National Park. This tranquil beach is ideal for long walks, birdwatching, and witnessing sea turtles nesting during the season. The nearby luxury resorts offer a peaceful retreat away from the crowds.

karonBeach.name: Karon Beach
karonBeach.description: Stretching over 3 kilometers, Karon Beach is one of Phuket’s longest and most peaceful beaches. The fine white sand produces a distinctive squeaking sound when you walk on it. The beach is less commercialized than Patong, offering a more relaxed atmosphere.

freedomBeach.name: Freedom Beach
freedomBeach.description: Accessible only by boat or a steep jungle trail, Freedom Beach is a hidden gem that rewards visitors with pristine white sand and crystal-clear waters. This secluded beach offers a tranquil escape from the crowds, perfect for swimming, sunbathing, and snorkeling.

naiHarnBeach.name: Nai Harn Beach
naiHarnBeach.description: Nestled in a quiet bay on Phuket’s southern coast, Nai Harn Beach is a favorite among locals and travelers seeking a more laid-back vibe. The beach is surrounded by lush greenery and offers calm waters ideal for swimming and paddleboarding.

naiYangBeach.name: Nai Yang Beach
naiYangBeach.description: Located within Sirinat National Park, Nai Yang Beach is a peaceful haven known for its natural beauty and turtle conservation efforts. The beach features soft sand, clear waters, and a relaxed atmosphere, making it perfect for families and nature lovers.

naiThonBeach.name: Nai Thon Beach
naiThonBeach.description: A quiet, crescent-shaped beach on Phuket’s northwest coast, Nai Thon offers a serene escape with soft sand and clear waters. The beach is ideal for swimming and relaxing, with a few beachfront restaurants serving fresh seafood.

rawaiBeach.name: Rawai Beach
rawaiBeach.description: Rawai Beach is a charming fishing village known for its seafood restaurants and vibrant local culture. While the beach itself is not ideal for swimming due to boat traffic, it serves as a gateway to nearby islands and offers stunning sunset views.

surinBeach.name: Surin Beach
surinBeach.description: Known as 'Millionaire’s Row' due to the luxury resorts and villas that line its shores, Surin Beach offers a sophisticated beach experience. The golden sand and clear waters are perfect for swimming and sunbathing, while the nearby beach clubs provide upscale dining and entertainment options.

kamalaBeach.name: Kamala Beach
kamalaBeach.description: A tranquil beach located north of Patong, Kamala is perfect for those seeking a quieter escape. The calm waters are ideal for swimming and stand-up paddleboarding. The beach is also home to Phuket FantaSea, a cultural theme park offering spectacular shows and entertainment.

bigBuddha.name: Big Buddha
bigBuddha.description: Standing 45 meters tall atop Nakkerd Hills, the Big Buddha is one of Phuket’s most revered landmarks. This massive white marble statue can be seen from miles away and offers breathtaking 360-degree views of the island. The best time to visit is during sunset when the statue glows golden.

watChalong.name: Wat Chalong
watChalong.description: Phuket’s largest and most important Buddhist temple, Wat Chalong is a stunning example of Thai religious architecture. The temple complex features ornate decorations, colorful murals depicting Buddha’s life, and a grand pagoda housing a bone fragment of Buddha.

promthepCape.name: Promthep Cape
promthepCape.description: Located at Phuket’s southernmost tip, Promthep Cape is famous for having the most spectacular sunsets on the island. This rocky promontory offers panoramic views of the Andaman Sea, with Koh Kew island visible in the distance.

karonViewpoint.name: Karon Viewpoint
karonViewpoint.description: Also known as Three Beaches Viewpoint, this scenic spot offers stunning vistas of three consecutive bays: Kata Noi, Kata Yai, and Karon Beach. Located on the hillside road between Nai Harn and Kata, it’s easily accessible and features parking areas and viewing platforms.

oldPhuketTown.name: Old Phuket Town
oldPhuketTown.description: A charming blend of Chinese and Portuguese colonial architecture, Old Phuket Town is the island’s cultural heart. Colorful Sino-Portuguese buildings line Thalang Road, Dibuk Road, and Yaowarat Road, now housing boutique hotels, art galleries, cafes, and restaurants.

phangNgaBay.name: Phang Nga Bay
phangNgaBay.description: A stunning seascape of limestone karsts rising dramatically from emerald waters, Phang Nga Bay is a geological wonder. Famous for James Bond Island (featured in "The Man with the Golden Gun"), the bay offers incredible kayaking through hidden lagoons and caves.

elephantSanctuary.name: Phuket Elephant Sanctuary
elephantSanctuary.description: Located in Paklok, the Phuket Elephant Sanctuary is the island’s first ethical elephant park. Visitors can observe rescued elephants roaming freely in lush natural surroundings. No riding or performances—just education, conservation, and compassion.

phiPhiIslands.name: Phi Phi Islands
phiPhiIslands.description: Made famous by "The Beach" movie, the Phi Phi Islands are a tropical paradise of crystal-clear waters, white sand beaches, and towering limestone cliffs. Activities include snorkeling in vibrant coral reefs, cliff jumping, beach hopping, and diving with leopard sharks.

fantasea.name: Phuket FantaSea
fantasea.description: Thailand’s ultimate cultural theme park, Phuket FantaSea combines Las Vegas-style entertainment with Thai mythology. The spectacular Palace of the Elephants show features traditional dance, aerial ballet, pyrotechnics, and a cast of elephants in an air-conditioned theater.

weekendMarket.name: Phuket Weekend Market
weekendMarket.description: Also known as Naka Market, this sprawling weekend market is where locals shop for everything from fresh produce to clothing and electronics. Open Saturday and Sunday evenings, it offers an authentic Thai market experience away from tourist areas.

phuket.byAirDesc: Phuket International Airport (HKT) receives direct flights from Bangkok (1 hour), Singapore, Hong Kong, Kuala Lumpur, and many other international destinations.
phuket.airportTransferDesc: Private transfers, taxis, and ride-sharing services are available at the airport. Many luxury villas offer complimentary airport pickup for guests.
phuket.gettingAroundDesc: Rent a car or scooter for flexibility, use Grab for convenient rides, or arrange private drivers through your villa for a hassle-free experience.

faqs.q1: What is the best time to visit Phuket?
faqs.a1: The best time to visit Phuket is from November to February during the cool, dry season when temperatures are comfortable (25-31°C) and rainfall is minimal.
faqs.q2: How do I get to Phuket?
faqs.a2: Phuket International Airport (HKT) is well-connected to major Asian cities and international destinations. Direct flights are available from Bangkok, Singapore, Hong Kong, and many other cities.
faqs.a3: Absolutely! Phuket offers family-friendly beaches like Kata and Karon, water parks, elephant sanctuaries, and numerous activities suitable for all ages.
faqs.q4: What currency is used in Phuket?
faqs.a4: Thai Baht (THB) is the local currency. Credit cards are widely accepted in hotels and restaurants, but cash is recommended for local markets and street vendors.

metadata.title: Pattaya | Silqhaus - Luxury Rentals & Beachfront Properties
metadata.description: Explore luxury vacation rentals in Pattaya, Thailand. Beachfront condos, private villas, and premium apartments await.

pattaya.title: Pattaya
pattaya.subtitle: Thailand’s premier beach resort city, where vibrant entertainment meets stunning coastlines and world-class attractions
pattaya.discoverP1: Once a quiet fishing village, Pattaya has transformed into Thailand’s most dynamic beach resort destination. Located just 150 kilometers southeast of Bangkok on the Eastern Gulf Coast, this vibrant city offers an incredible mix of entertainment, culture, and natural beauty.
pattaya.discoverP2: Beyond its famous nightlife scene, Pattaya surprises visitors with world-class attractions like the awe-inspiring Sanctuary of Truth, the spectacular Nong Nooch Tropical Garden, and pristine island escapes just a short boat ride away.
pattaya.discoverP3: Our luxury villas in Pattaya offer the perfect retreat after exploring the city’s many attractions. Enjoy private pools, stunning views, and the finest Thai hospitality in exclusive residential settings.
pattaya.attractionsSubtitle: Explore the best attractions Pattaya has to offer

jomtienBeach.name: Jomtien Beach
jomtienBeach.description: A family-friendly beach stretching 6 kilometers south of Pattaya, Jomtien offers a more relaxed atmosphere than the main beach. The calm waters are perfect for swimming, jet skiing, parasailing, and beach volleyball. Palm-lined shores provide natural shade, and the beachfront promenade is dotted with seafood restaurants and massage pavilions.

pattayaBeach.name: Pattaya Beach
pattayaBeach.description: The iconic 4-kilometer crescent-shaped beach is the heart of Pattaya’s coastal scene. While the water quality varies, the beach offers stunning sunset views and easy access to the city’s vibrant nightlife on Walking Street. Beach bars, water sports vendors, and comfortable sun loungers line the sandy shore.

kohLarn.name: Koh Larn (Coral Island)
kohLarn.description: Just 40 minutes by ferry from Bali Hai Pier, Koh Larn offers the crystal-clear turquoise waters that Pattaya’s mainland beaches lack. This tropical paradise features six pristine beaches, with Tawaen and Samae being the most popular. Enjoy snorkeling, banana boat rides, and fresh seafood at beachside restaurants.

sanctuaryOfTruth.name: Sanctuary of Truth
sanctuaryOfTruth.description: A breathtaking 105-meter tall temple made entirely of wood without a single nail. This architectural masterpiece features intricate hand-carved sculptures depicting Buddhist, Hindu, and Chinese mythology. Started in 1981 and still under construction, it stands majestically on the oceanfront. Traditional Thai cultural performances are held daily.

bigBuddha.name: Wat Phra Yai (Big Buddha)
bigBuddha.description: Perched atop Pratumnak Hill, this 18-meter golden Buddha statue has been watching over Pattaya Bay since the 1940s. The temple offers panoramic 360-degree views of the city and coastline. Visitors can receive blessings from monks, ring bells for good luck, and explore the peaceful temple grounds. Entry is free with donations welcome.

nongNooch.name: Nong Nooch Tropical Garden
nongNooch.description: Southeast Asia’s largest botanical garden spanning 600 acres of beautifully landscaped grounds. Marvel at tropical flowers, themed gardens including French, Stonehenge, and dinosaur valleys, plus traditional Thai houses. Daily cultural shows feature elephant performances and Thai dancing. A full day is needed to explore this horticultural wonderland.

ramayanaWaterPark.name: Ramayana Water Park
ramayanaWaterPark.description: Thailand’s largest water park and ranked among Asia’s best, Ramayana features over 21 thrilling slides, a 600-meter lazy river, and a massive wave pool. Set against a backdrop of Thai mythology-themed architecture, it offers attractions for all ages from gentle family pools to heart-pumping drop slides. Open daily with full-day and half-day passes available.

floatingMarket.name: Pattaya Floating Market
floatingMarket.description: A unique cultural attraction featuring over 100 traditional wooden shops and restaurants built on waterways. Representing all four regions of Thailand, vendors sell authentic handicrafts, souvenirs, and delicious street food. Take a boat ride through the canals or walk along the wooden pathways. Traditional dance performances and live music add to the atmosphere.

nightMarket.name: Thepprasit Night Market
nightMarket.description: A sprawling weekend market where locals shop for everything from fresh produce to electronics. Open Friday through Sunday evenings, it offers an authentic Thai market experience away from tourist areas. Hundreds of food stalls serve southern Thai specialties, grilled seafood, and fresh tropical fruits at local prices.

pattaya.fromBangkokDesc: Regular buses depart from Ekkamai Bus Station (2 hours, ~150 THB) and Mo Chit. Private taxis and ride-sharing services take about 1.5-2 hours depending on traffic and cost 1,500-2,000 THB.
pattaya.byAirDesc: Most visitors fly into Bangkok’s Suvarnabhumi Airport and take ground transport to Pattaya.
pattaya.gettingAroundDesc: Songthaews (baht buses) run fixed routes for 10-20 THB. Grab is widely available for convenience. Motorbike and car rentals are popular for exploring nearby attractions independently.

faqs.q1: What is the best time to visit Pattaya?
faqs.a1: The best time to visit Pattaya is from November to February during the cool, dry season. Temperatures are comfortable (25-32°C) with minimal rainfall. The monsoon season runs from May to October with occasional heavy showers.
faqs.q2: How do I get to Pattaya from Bangkok?
faqs.a2: Pattaya is just 2 hours from Bangkok by bus (around 150 THB). Regular buses depart from Ekkamai and Mo Chit bus stations. Private taxis cost around 1,500-2,000 THB. U-Tapao Airport near Pattaya also has limited international flights.
faqs.a3: Yes! Pattaya offers many family-friendly attractions including Ramayana Water Park, Nong Nooch Garden, Underwater World aquarium, and the peaceful beaches of Jomtien. Many resorts cater specifically to families with kids’ clubs and pools.
faqs.q4: What is the local transportation in Pattaya?
faqs.a4: Songthaews (shared pickup trucks) are the most common transport, costing 10-20 THB within the city. Motorbike taxis are quick for short trips. Grab is widely available, and car rentals are popular for exploring nearby attractions.
